input.rationale: First substantive product of this run: a partial but usable map of the EPaxos replica responsibility (core_overview for both core relationships, seven activities, sixteen behaviors, seven facts, ten surfaced unread boundaries) plus the first Candidate. The map is sourced only from the captured snapshot; all anomalies found while tracing the backbone are retained as open_details instead of being asserted as defects. The Candidate selects the one sourced discrepancy that would matter most if reachable: handlePreAccept stores a received command into InstanceSpace[PreAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler addresses the instance (PreAccept.Replica, Instance) named by the message.

question.question: When a replica receives PreAccept for instance (Replica, Instance) while its local record for that instance already has Status >= ACCEPTED but stores no commands, handlePreAccept writes the received command into InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] instead of the addressed instance InstanceSpace[preAccept.Replica][Instance]. Is any legal history able to put a replica in that state with preAccept.LeaderId != preAccept.Replica, and if so does the addressed record (Replica, Instance) stay without commands (halting its row's execution and the recovery replies about it) while an unrelated record (LeaderId, Instance) acquires a command that no quorum committed for it?
question.importance: Wrong-slot attribution of a command mutates protocol state without any quorum behind it: a record that never committed that command can become executable as though it had, while the record the message was addressed to can be left permanently unexecutable because executeCommands requires Cmds != nil and findSCC returns false for a command-less instance. Both effects are consensus-visible (an uncommitted command can reach the state machine, and a committed instance can stop making progress).
contexts: instance owned by replica R and led by replica L != R (recovery re-proposal)
instance owned and led by the same replica (normal proposal) as the control that must behave identically
event_paths: deliver PreAccept(LeaderId=L, Replica=R, Instance=i, Ballot=b, Command=c, Seq, Deps) to a replica whose InstanceSpace[R][i] has Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil
compare the record that receives Cmds after the handler returns against the record named by (Replica, Instance)

supporting_behavior_ids.B5-slow-path-accept: shows that the accept phase stores accepted attributes on followers without any status transition, which is the premise the >= ACCEPTED branch would need
supporting_behavior_ids.B11-prepare-resolution: re-runs pre-accept on behalf of another replica's instance, which is the only read path in which PreAccept.LeaderId differs from PreAccept.Replica
supporting_behavior_ids.B12-try-preaccept: another recovery path that re-sends a command for an instance owned by a different replica
supporting_behavior_ids.B7-execute-scheduler: shows the execution requirement Cmds != nil that makes a command-less record of the addressed instance a permanent row stall

counterevidence: no read path found so far sets Status >= ACCEPTED together with Cmds == nil on a replica that did not already hold the command: leader-side transitions copy lb.cmds, handleCommit copies commit.Command, and a nil Command does not survive the wire format as nil (S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit)
handleAccept deliberately stores accepted attributes without a status transition, which would make the branch unreachable for acceptors rather than wrong (S11-handleAccept)
unknowns: whether any in-repository path (for example a recovery that commits an instance for which no replica reported a command) can leave Status >= ACCEPTED with Cmds == nil at a replica
whether the branch was intended to address the instance owner and the LeaderId index is the only wrong part, or whether the accepted-state condition is also wrong
whether an executor can observe the wrong-slot write, since executeCommands requires Cmds != nil and Status == COMMITTED for the affected record
question.trigger_rationale: Source reading showed the discrepancy directly: S9-handlePreAccept uses preAccept.Replica at lines 782, 792-798, 810, 816 and 828-829, but preAccept.LeaderId at line 809 for the same object. The state needed to reach the branch (Status >= ACCEPTED with nil Cmds on a replica receiving a PreAccept) is not obviously produced by any path read so far: handleAccept stores bal/vbal/Seq/Deps without recording ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept), the leader-side ACCEPTED/COMMITTED transitions set Cmds from lb.cmds (S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S12-handleAcceptReply), handleCommit installs commit.Command (S13-handleCommit), and a marshalled nil command slice comes back as a non-nil empty slice. The Candidate therefore fixes the reachability premise as the discriminator rather than assuming the defect is triggered.

result.summary:
First product of this run: a sourced partial map plus the first Candidate for the EPaxos replica in the captured swiftpaxos snapshot.

What was done. I read the epaxos package (epaxos.go, exec.go, defs.go) and the shared helpers it depends on (replica/replica.go quorum sizes and listeners, replica/defs, state/state.go, run.go launch wiring), then traced both core lines end to end: command admission -> startPhase1 attribute derivation -> PreAccept on receivers -> reply merge -> fast-path commit or majority Accept -> Commit install, and ballot promise/raise (bal, vbal, maxRecvBallot, makeBallot) -> execution-timeout driven recovery -> prepare over a slow quorum -> highest-vbal value selection -> accept / try-preAccept / phase-1 restart, including how committed records short-circuit recovery, how lower-ballot messages are dropped, and how pending client proposals survive a leader change. The map records 7 activities, 16 behaviors, 7 facts, target profile, and 7 surfaced unread boundaries, with the overview marked usable and the anomalies kept as open_details rather than asserted as defects.

First Candidate. handlePreAccept is the only handler that addresses an instance two ways: it reads and writes InstanceSpace[preAccept.Replica][Instance] at lines 782, 792-798, 810, 816 and 828-829, but at line 809 stores the received command into InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance]. If any legal history reaches that branch (local Status >= ACCEPTED with nil Cmds) while LeaderId != Replica, the addressed record (Replica, Instance) is left command-less (executeCommands requires Cmds != nil, so its row halts) and an unrelated record (LeaderId, Instance) gains a command no quorum committed for it. The Candidate deliberately fixes the unresolved premise as its discriminator: reading found no path that produces Status >= ACCEPTED with nil Cmds (handleAccept stores bal/vbal/Seq/Deps but records no ACCEPTED status; leader-side transitions copy lb.cmds; a nil Command does not survive the wire format as nil), so reachability is the open question, not the discrepancy itself. Counterevidence and both interpretations are retained.

Other sourced anomalies were recorded as open_details only (identical guards for handlePrepareReply sub-cases 3 and 4; the defer-cycle guard counting lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] in a loop over q; the stable-store header writing bal and vbal into the same bytes with no reader; the inert transconf block; the N<=3 with Thrifty equality exemption). Local compilation of ./epaxos with the captured module cache succeeds, so a controlled in-package harness (replicas wired through in-memory peer writers) is feasible for the next step; no formal check was submitted this turn.

materials.text:
type Replica struct {
	*replica.Replica
	prepareChan           chan fastrpc.Serializable
	preAcceptChan         chan fastrpc.Serializable
	acceptChan            chan fastrpc.Serializable
	commitChan            chan fastrpc.Serializable
	prepareReplyChan      chan fastrpc.Serializable
	preAcceptReplyChan    chan fastrpc.Serializable
	preAcceptOKChan       chan fastrpc.Serializable
	acceptReplyChan       chan fastrpc.Serializable
	tryPreAcceptChan      chan fastrpc.Serializable
	tryPreAcceptReplyChan chan fastrpc.Serializable
	prepareRPC            uint8
	prepareReplyRPC       uint8
	preAcceptRPC          uint8
	preAcceptReplyRPC     uint8
	acceptRPC             uint8
	acceptReplyRPC        uint8
	commitRPC             uint8
	tryPreAcceptRPC       uint8
	tryPreAcceptReplyRPC  uint8
	// the space of all instances (used and not yet used)
	InstanceSpace [][]*Instance
	// highest active instance numbers that this replica knows about
	crtInstance []int32
	// highest committed instance per replica that this replica knows about
	CommittedUpTo []int32
	// instance up to which all commands have been executed (including iteslf)
	ExecedUpTo       []int32
	exec             *Exec
	conflicts        []map[state.Key]*InstPair
	maxSeqPerKey     map[state.Key]int32
	maxSeq           int32
	latestCPReplica  int32
	latestCPInstance int32
	// for synchronizing when sending replies to clients
	// from multiple go-routines
	clientMutex        *sync.Mutex
	instancesToRecover chan *instanceId
	// does this replica think it is the leader
	IsLeader      bool
	maxRecvBallot int32
	batchWait     int
	transconf     bool
}

type Instance struct {
	Cmds           []state.Command
	bal, vbal      int32
	Status         int8
	Seq            int32
	Deps           []int32
	lb             *LeaderBookkeeping
	Index, Lowlink int
	bfilter        any
	proposeTime    int64
	id             *instanceId
}

type instanceId struct {
	replica  int32
	instance int32
}

type LeaderBookkeeping struct {
	clientProposals   []*defs.GPropose
	ballot            int32
	allEqual          bool
	preAcceptOKs      int
	acceptOKs         int
	nacks             int
	originalDeps      []int32
	committedDeps     []int32
	prepareReplies    []*PrepareReply
	preparing         bool
	tryingToPreAccept bool
	possibleQuorum    []bool
	tpaReps           int
	tpaAccepted       bool
	lastTriedBallot   int32
	cmds              []state.Command
	status            int8
	seq               int32
	deps              []int32
	leaderResponded   bool
}

func (r *Replica) run() {
	r.ConnectToPeers()

	r.ComputeClosestPeers()

	if r.Exec {
		go r.executeCommands()
	}

	slowClockChan = make(chan bool, 1)
	fastClockChan = make(chan bool, 1)
	go r.slowClock()

	if r.BatchingEnabled() {
		go r.fastClock()
	}

	if r.Beacon {
		go r.stopAdapting()
	}

	onOffProposeChan := r.ProposeChan

	go r.WaitForClientConnections()

	for !r.Shutdown {

		select {

		case propose := <-onOffProposeChan:
			r.handlePropose(propose)
			if r.BatchingEnabled() {
				onOffProposeChan = nil
			}
			break

		case <-fastClockChan:
			onOffProposeChan = r.ProposeChan
			break

		case prepareS := <-r.prepareChan:
			prepare := prepareS.(*Prepare)
			r.handlePrepare(prepare)
			break

		case preAcceptS := <-r.preAcceptChan:
			preAccept := preAcceptS.(*PreAccept)
			r.handlePreAccept(preAccept)
			break

		case acceptS := <-r.acceptChan:
			accept := acceptS.(*Accept)
			r.handleAccept(accept)
			break

		case commitS := <-r.commitChan:
			commit := commitS.(*Commit)
			r.handleCommit(commit)
			break

		case prepareReplyS := <-r.prepareReplyChan:
			prepareReply := prepareReplyS.(*PrepareReply)
			r.handlePrepareReply(prepareReply)
			break

		case preAcceptReplyS := <-r.preAcceptReplyChan:
			preAcceptReply := preAcceptReplyS.(*PreAcceptReply)
			r.handlePreAcceptReply(preAcceptReply)
			break

		case acceptReplyS := <-r.acceptReplyChan:
			acceptReply := acceptReplyS.(*AcceptReply)
			r.handleAcceptReply(acceptReply)
			break

		case tryPreAcceptS := <-r.tryPreAcceptChan:
			tryPreAccept := tryPreAcceptS.(*TryPreAccept)
			r.handleTryPreAccept(tryPreAccept)
			break

		case tryPreAcceptReplyS := <-r.tryPreAcceptReplyChan:
			tryPreAcceptReply := tryPreAcceptReplyS.(*TryPreAcceptReply)
			r.handleTryPreAcceptReply(tryPreAcceptReply)
			break

		case beacon := <-r.BeaconChan:
			r.ReplyBeacon(beacon)
			break

		case <-slowClockChan:
			if r.Beacon {
				r.Printf("weird %d; conflicted %d; slow %d; fast %d\n", r.Stats.M["weird"], r.Stats.M["conflicted"], r.Stats.M["slow"], r.Stats.M["fast"])
				for q := int32(0); q < int32(r.N); q++ {
					if q == r.Id {
						continue
					}
					r.SendBeacon(q)
				}
			}
			break

		case iid := <-r.instancesToRecover:
			r.startRecoveryForInstance(iid.replica, iid.instance)
		}
	}
}

func runReplica(c *config.Config, logger *dlog.Logger) {
	port := c.Port

	log.Printf("Server starting on port %d", port)
	maddr := fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", c.MasterAddr, c.MasterPort)
	addr := c.ReplicaAddrs[c.Alias]
	replicaId, nodeList, isLeader := registerWithMaster(addr, maddr, port)
	f := (len(c.ReplicaAddrs) - 1) / 2
	log.Printf("Tolerating %d max. failures", f)

	switch strings.ToLower(c.Protocol) {
	case "swiftpaxos":
		log.Println("Starting SwiftPaxos replica...")
		swift.MaxDescRoutines = 100
		rep := swift.New(c.Alias, replicaId, nodeList, !c.Noop,
			c.Optread, true, false, 1, f, c, logger, nil)
		rpc.Register(rep)
	case "curp":
		log.Println("Starting optimized CURP replica...")
		curp.MaxDescRoutines = 100
		rep := curp.New(c.Alias, replicaId, nodeList, !c.Noop,
			1, f, true, c, logger)
		rpc.Register(rep)
	case "fastpaxos":
		log.Println("Starting Fast Paxos replica...")
		rep := fastpaxos.New(c.Alias, replicaId, nodeList, !c.Noop, f, c, logger)
		rpc.Register(rep)
	case "n2paxos":
		log.Println("Starting N²Paxos replica...")
		rep := n2paxos.New(c.Alias, replicaId, nodeList, !c.Noop, 1, f, c, logger)
		rpc.Register(rep)
	case "paxos":
		log.Println("Starting Paxos replica...")
		rep := paxos.New(c.Alias, replicaId, nodeList, isLeader, f, c, logger)
		rpc.Register(rep)
	case "epaxos":
		log.Println("Starting EPaxos replica...")
		rep := epaxos.New(c.Alias, replicaId, nodeList, !c.Noop, false, false, 0, false, f, c, logger)
		rpc.Register(rep)
	}

	rpc.HandleHTTP()
	l, err := net.Listen("tcp", fmt.Sprintf(":%d", port+1000))
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal("listen error:", err)
	}
	http.Serve(l, nil)
}

SwiftPaxos: Fast Geo-Replicated State Machines
==========
<!-- [![Go Report Card](https://goreportcard.com/badge/github.com/imdea-software/swiftpaxos)](https://goreportcard.com/report/github.com/imdea-software/swiftpaxos) -->

This repository contains the prototype implementation of SwiftPaxos, a new state-machine replication protocol for geo-distributed systems.
SwiftPaxos is a _faster Paxos without compromises_.
In the best case, it executes a state-machine command in two message delays (one round-trip), and three otherwise.
SwiftPaxos was [presented](https://www.usenix.org/conference/nsdi24/presentation/ryabinin) at the 21st USENIX Symposium on Networked Systems Design and Implementation ([NSDI '24](https://www.usenix.org/conference/nsdi24)).

Installation
------------

    git clone https://github.com/imdea-software/swiftpaxos.git
    cd swiftpaxos
    go install github.com/imdea-software/swiftpaxos

Implemented protocols
---------------------

|  Protocol               | Comments                                          |
|-------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| SwiftPaxos              | See our NSDI'24 [paper](https://www.usenix.org/conference/nsdi24/presentation/ryabinin) for the full details.|
| Paxos                   | The classic Paxos protocol.                       |
| N<sup>2</sup>Paxos      | All-to-all variant of Paxos.                      |
| CURP                    | CURP implemented over N<sup>2</sup>Paxos.         |
| Fast Paxos              | Fast Paxos with uncoordinated collision recovery. |
| EPaxos                  | A [corrected][epaxos_correct] version of EPaxos.  |

This software is based on the [Egalitarian Paxos](https://github.com/otrack/epaxos) code base, as well as the corrections made [here](https://github.com/otrack/epaxos).

Usage
-----
#### participants
There are three types of participants: *master*, *servers* and *clients*. 
The servers and clients implement the protocol logic. 
The master maintains the configuration of the system.

#### deployment configuration
To setup a run, the participants read deployment configuration file. 
See [aws.conf][config] for an example of configuration file for AWS EC2.

#### launching a participant

Master:
    
    swiftpaxos -run master -config conf.conf

Server:

    swiftpaxos -run server -config conf.conf -alias server_name

Client:

    swiftpaxos -run client -config conf.conf -alias client_name

#### command line options

    -alias alias
        An alias of this participant
    -config file

selections.rationale: First substantive product of this run: a partial but usable map of the EPaxos replica responsibility (core_overview for both core relationships, seven activities, sixteen behaviors, seven facts, ten surfaced unread boundaries) plus the first Candidate. The map is sourced only from the captured snapshot; all anomalies found while tracing the backbone are retained as open_details instead of being asserted as defects. The Candidate selects the one sourced discrepancy that would matter most if reachable: handlePreAccept stores a received command into InstanceSpace[PreAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler addresses the instance (PreAccept.Replica, Instance) named by the message.

after.purpose: Form a per-instance decision: fix the command, its sequence number and its dependency vector, and advance the instance from tentative pre-accept through accept to commit.
after.realization_summary: handlePropose allocates (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq,deps) from the local conflict tables, records the instance as PREACCEPTED and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers (Thrifty). handlePreAccept recomputes attributes on the receiver and replies with (bal,vbal,seq,deps,CommittedUpTo,status). handlePreAcceptReply merges replies and commits on the fast path when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and allEqual and (for N>7) allCommitted and the ballot is the initial ballot; otherwise the instance moves to ACCEPTED and a majority accept round runs in handleAcceptReply (acceptOKs+1 > N/2), followed by bcastCommit.
variants: Thrifty fast quorum versus full broadcast
N<=3 and Thrifty skip the attribute-equality check
N>7 propagates committedDeps and can make the fast path fail on allCommitted
batching when batchWait > 0 (disabled by run.go)
unknowns: whether skipping the equality check for N<=3 with Thrifty is compensated by another mechanism

after.purpose: Carry the per-instance authority context: which ballot the record is promised to, at which ballot its attributes were last fixed, and which replica may currently advance it.
after.realization_summary: Each Instance keeps bal (highest ballot promised) and vbal (ballot at which the current attributes were established). maxRecvBallot is raised by every received message type and constrains makeBallot, which picks id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and further raised while IsLeader. Ballot comparison gates every message and reply: lower ballots are dropped or nacked, and a majority of nacks lets a replica raise the ballot and run prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead it does.
variants: initial ballot equals the owner replica id
recovery ballot for a non-owner is shifted by N
unknowns: whether any in-repository caller other than a nack majority ever sets IsLeader

after.purpose: Re-establish eligible participation for an instance that is blocking execution by reconstructing its attributes and value from a majority.
after.realization_summary: executeCommands times out an instance that has stayed uncommittable for COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD (10s) and pushes instancesToRecover; startRecoveryForInstance returns early when the local record is already committed with commands, otherwise it seeds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record and broadcasts Prepare. handlePrepareReply waits for SlowQuorumSize replies at the current ballot, takes the attributes of the highest vbal and selects sub-case 1..6 (already committed, accepted, pre-accepted with enough equal support, weaker pre-accepted support, restart phase 1 with the recovered or NOOP command).
variants: sub-case dispatch order documented in handlePrepareReply
TryPreAccept path started from sub-case 4
defer-cycle guard using possibleQuorum
unknowns: which sub-case condition the comment lines describe, given that sub-cases 3 and 4 carry identical guards today

after.purpose: Define participant eligibility and quorum arithmetic: who is a member, who is believed alive, and how many equal or majority supports are needed.
after.realization_summary: N and F come from the peer address list and the master-visible participant count; FastQuorumSize = F + (F+1)/2, SlowQuorumSize = (N+1)/2, WriteQuorumSize = F+1, ReadQuorumSize = N-F. Alive[] is set during connection setup and cleared by replicaListener when a peer reader fails; PreferredPeerOrder (from ComputeClosestPeers or the latency table) decides which FastQuorumSize-1 peers and which majority peers receive PreAccept/Accept/Commit.
variants: Thrifty subset selection versus full broadcast
injected per-peer delays from the latency file
unknowns: whether a peer whose reader failed is ever re-admitted, since Alive is only cleared in the listener

after.purpose: Apply committed instances to the replicated state machine in one order and complete the client-visible operation.
after.realization_summary: executeCommands scans rows in replica order and instances in increasing order from ExecedUpTo+1, requires Status == COMMITTED, computes the strongly connected component of the dependency graph reachable from the candidate, and executes every instance of that component in increasing (Seq, owner replica, proposeTime) order; each executed instance is marked EXECUTED and ExecedUpTo advances only over contiguous prefixes. Client replies are produced during execution when a proposal is still attached (Dreply true), otherwise at commit time.
variants: transconf block in strongconnect (inert as written)
Dreply true (replies on execute) versus false (replies on commit)
unknowns: whether per-row ordering of non-conflicting commands is required by any consumer

after.purpose: Retain the local history later decisions depend on: per-key conflict indexes, watermarks, and when enabled a durable record.
after.realization_summary: conflicts[q][key] holds last (any op) and lastWrite (non-GET) instance numbers per replica, and maxSeqPerKey holds the highest sequence seen per key; both are updated at proposal, at pre-accept on the receiver and at commit. CommittedUpTo and ExecedUpTo are contiguous-prefix watermarks over the instance rows. recordInstanceMetadata/recordCommands/sync write a stable-store record when Durable is set; run.go always passes durable = false.
variants: Durable false (launched configuration) makes the stable-store path inert
conflict tables are never cleared after process start
unknowns: no reader of the stable store exists in the captured snapshot, so the record layout has no in-repo consumer

after.purpose: Define when a client-visible operation is complete and how a proposal survives a leader or replica change.
after.realization_summary: A client connection writes Propose records into a delayed channel; the replica attaches the writer, mutex and proxy flag to a GPropose and answers either during execution (Dreply true) or at commit (!Dreply), using ReplyProposeTS with the original CommandId and Timestamp. Pending proposals are kept in LeaderBookkeeping.clientProposals so a recovered instance can still answer them, and a NOOP commit on the owner's own row re-proposes the pending proposals onto ProposeChan.
variants: Dreply true versus false
NOOP re-proposal only when commit.Replica == r.Id
unknowns: whether a client can observe a reply for a proposal whose command was replaced by NOOP

after.trigger: a GPropose arrives on ProposeChan from clientListener through the delayed propose channel
legal_preconditions: the client connection is registered so a reply writer exists
implementation_guards: batching drains len(ProposeChan)+1 proposals when BatchingEnabled, otherwise one proposal

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept); which histories reach that branch is unresolved.

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

handlePrepareReply documents six sub-cases but the guards for sub-cases 3 and 4 are textually identical, so the TryPreAccept-based sub-case appears unreachable (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept).
handleTryPreAcceptReply's defer-cycle guard counts lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] inside a loop over q, so the count can only be 0 or N and never equals N/2 (S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

recordInstanceMetadata writes bal and vbal into the same [0:4] byte range and stores Status at offset 4 inside a 9+4N header, and no reader of that format exists in the snapshot; the launcher always passes durable = false (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos).
the transconf branch inside Exec.strongconnect computes state.Conflict but performs no action, and run.go passes transconf = false (S20-exec, S24-runReplica-epaxos).
the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1 (S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S21-quorum-sizes).
after.rationale: Both core relationships are traced through real entry points (client propose to phase 1 to pre-accept replies to fast or slow decision to commit install, and ballot promise to nack-driven prepare to recovery sub-cases) and their connection is stated in terms of the per-instance record, the highest-vbal reply rule, the committed short-circuit and the ballot comparison that rejects old replies. The remaining questions are local anomalies inside handlers rather than missing formation, authority-transition or old-work handling, so the overview is recorded as usable with those anomalies kept as open_details and as the first Candidate's discriminator.
